mismatch.message: simple monster action requires uhitm.c mhitm_ad_corr()

summary: A black pudding bites the hero, but the AD_CORR dispatch refuses mhitm_ad_corr before completing the turn. C corrodes the worn chain mail. Port the whole helper and its required armor-erosion return chain.

source.branch: A successful AT_BITE/AD_CORR monster-to-hero hit with an uncancelled black pudding and worn chain mail reaches erode_armor(ERODE_CORRODE).

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:2338-2361 defines the whole mhitm_ad_corr helper. Hero-to-monster erodes armor and clears damage; monster-to-hero prints hitmsg and skips erosion when cancelled; monster-to-monster skips when cancelled, otherwise erodes armor, clears STRAT_WAITFORU, and clears damage.

nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:126-185 erode_armor retries rn2(5) until an eligible helmet, shield, gloves, or boots target changes, while the body case tries cloak, suit, then shirt and terminates. It consumes which_armor, xname, and erode_obj results. Resolve their complete source-backed return dependencies rather than introducing a fixed target or draw.

js/uhitm.js:4958 dispatches AD_CORR to unported(mhitm_ad_corr); a search for function erode_armor in js found no body. The admitted baseline stops at zero-based segment 0 step 67 with simple monster action requires uhitm.c mhitm_ad_corr().

The frozen C recording at segment 0 step 67 contains rnd(20)=5 at mattacku, d(3,8)=17 at hitmu, then rn2(5)=1 at erode_armor and the screen The black pudding bites! Your chain mail corrodes!--More--. These prove the attack and body-slot corrosion route, not just a generic monster-turn RNG annotation.

The first missing comparator call is distfleeck(monmove.c:538). C makes it before the attack in this turn; the JS preflight refusal prevents the entire turn boundary. It is a reporting symptom, not evidence that distfleeck needs a special draw. Scope includes all three actor combinations of mhitm_ad_corr and required helper/caller wiring; no completion credit for the whole outer mattacku or hitmu functions.
